summary: Fix 7 (portion-scaling guard + prompt rewrite + energy_source tolerance) fully verified. New pytest module test_fix7_portion_scaling.py adds 23 unit tests: 5 archetypes (yogurt, Youfoodz, beef mince, eggs, milk) exercising enforce_portion_scaling across per-serving misreads, per-100g misreads, correctly-scaled inputs, close-enough label energies, and grossly-wrong energy corrections; plus 8 no-op / edge-case tests (per_100g=None, all-zero, portion<=0, portion<0, impossible per_100g logs skip, correction log shape includes name+per_100g+X→Y deltas, protein_g/carbs_g/fat_g alias variants); plus 4 sanitize_food_entry Fix-1 tolerance-branching tests proving energy_source='label' honours 12% while 'derived'/missing honour 10%. Each archetype test runs the guard 5x and asserts identical output — determinism confirmed. Regression: total 104/104 pass across Fix7 (23) + nutrition-accuracy guard (58) + Fix5 egg-weight (23) in 20.68s. Zero regressions. Compact before/after table printed at end of Fix7 run for user's pre/post comparison (see test_zzz_print_before_after_table). Integration test against /food/log intentionally skipped — FoodLogRequest does NOT accept per_100g or energy_source fields (Pydantic strips unknowns), so enforce_portion_scaling is unreachable via /food/log; the review request explicitly acknowledged this is intentional (portion-scaling belongs to /food/analyze which reads labels). Fix-1 tolerance branching still works on any dict passed to sanitize_food_entry directly, verified by 4 dedicated unit tests.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py line 8347: enforce_portion_scaling uses `energy_source == 'label'` (case-sensitive). analyze_food_image already lowercases the incoming value (line 8547 `_energy_source = str(...).lower()`) so this works end-to-end, but any external caller passing 'LABEL' or 'Label' directly to the helper would fall through to the 10% derived tolerance. Non-blocking; consider lowercasing inside the helper for defence-in-depth.
server.py line 8363: correction stores `int(round(exp))` for calories and `round(exp, 2)` for macros. Egg archetype protein result is 29.23 (12.6 * 2.32 = 29.232) — this matches. Good.
server.py line 8332: rejects per_100g when protein/carbs/fats > 100. Calories >100 per 100g is legitimate (e.g. oil = 900cal/100g), so calories are correctly excluded from the ceiling check. Good.

rca_of_issue: N/A — this iteration verifies newly-added Fix 7 deterministic portion-scaling guard. Root cause of the systemic defect (per user report): Vision model copied the label's per-serving row verbatim without applying the user's portion multiplier, producing 24% under-count on 180g yogurt scan (85 cal reported vs 112 cal correct). Fix: (a) prompt rewritten to demand explicit per_100g + portion_g fields + energy_source enum, (b) new pure-math enforce_portion_scaling helper computes expected = per_100g × portion_g/100 and overwrites any macro >10% off (12% for label-transcribed calories to accommodate Atwater deltas), (c) helper invoked in analyze_food_image after sanitize+retry, before quantity multiplier, (d) sanitize_food_entry Fix-1 tolerance widened to 12% when energy_source='label' so label calories aren't clobbered. All four fix legs verified: prompt strings present in server.py, helper deterministic across 5 trials × 5 archetypes, tolerance branching correct at 11%/13% boundary values, and the retry+guard+sanitize chain preserved in analyze_food_image.
